subject: Computer Networking
title: Ports: Which App Gets the Data?
description: A quick win: understand Ports: Which App Gets the Data?.

hook.text: Your computer runs a browser, email, and a game — all using the internet. How does each get the right data?

buildup.text: Every network connection uses a port number. It's like an apartment number inside an IP address building.

discovery.text: Web traffic uses port 80 or 443. Email uses 25 or 587. Each service claims its own door.

twist.text: Your browser opens a random high port for each tab. The server replies to that specific port, not just your IP.

climax.text: Firewalls control access by port. Block port 22 and nobody can SSH in, even if they know the IP.

punchline.text: IP gets data to the machine. Ports get it to the app.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of port numbers in networking?
options: To direct traffic to the correct application on a device
To assign IP addresses to devices

details.summary: Ports are numerical identifiers that direct incoming data to the correct application on a device. While the IP address identifies the device, the port identifies which program should receive the data. HTTP uses port 80, HTTPS uses 443, and applications can use any of 65,535 available ports.
details.whyItMatters: Ports allow a single device to run many networked applications simultaneously. Without ports, a computer could only communicate with one service at a time.
takeaways: Ports identify which application should receive incoming data
Well-known ports: HTTP is 80, HTTPS is 443, SSH is 22
There are 65,535 available ports per protocol

faq.question: What is the difference between well-known and ephemeral ports?
faq.answer: Well-known ports are 0 to 1023, reserved for standard services like HTTP and SSH. Registered ports are 1024 to 49151 for specific applications. Ephemeral ports, 49152 to 65535, are assigned temporarily by the OS for outgoing connections. The client uses an ephemeral port to receive responses.

faq.question: Why do firewalls block certain ports?
faq.answer: Firewalls block ports to prevent unauthorized access to services. An open port means a program is listening for connections. Leaving unnecessary ports open creates attack surface. Firewalls typically allow only ports 80 and 443 for web traffic and block everything else by default.
